sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: MLLT6 is a chromatin-associated transcriptional regulator that interacts with histone-modifying machinery. One of its best-characterized functions is interaction with the DOT1L/DOT1A H3K79 methyltransferase complex, where MLLT6 competes with AF9 and can alter DOT1L localization and H3K79 methylation levels (Reisenauer et al. (2009)).

sections.heading: Pathway

paragraphs.suffix: (MLLT6, DOT1L, KMT2D, TP63, IRF6, GRHL3). MLLT6 is positioned upstream of DOT1L as a chromatin-associated regulator that may facilitate DOT1L-dependent H3K79 methylation. This epigenetic module is hypothesized to support transcriptional programs required for epithelial differentiation and integrity, thereby influencing developmental pathways that converge on the TP63-IRF6-GRHL3 network during palatogenesis.

paragraphs: The pathway proposes that both the KMT2D and MLLT6-DOT1L modules act as positive regulators of the TP63 developmental program. While KMT2D contributes enhancer activation and DOT1L contributes H3K79 methylation-associated transcriptional activity, both pathways are predicted to converge on maintenance of TP63-dependent epithelial differentiation, including the downstream IRF6-GRHL3 axis.
